clue.text: Mystic's rejected medicine — one swallowed by a chap

indicators.note: rejected suggests something sent back, so the medicine word is read backwards

parts.note: a drug is a medicine

indicators.note: swallowed by places the numeral inside the man's name, as food goes inside a body

parts.note: Jeff is a typical man's name, standing for any chap
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A mystic turns down medicine, and somebody gulps down a pill.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link ('is'). G. I. Gurdjieff was an Armenian-born spiritual teacher of the early twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Gurdjieff was a famous esoteric teacher, an example of a mystic.

clue.text: A cheesy device that's off target

clue.text: Torture device to hire in an Irish castle

parts.note: the rack is a medieval instrument of torture that stretches its victim
to rent is to hire

explanation.surface: An instrument of torture is to be hired in an Irish castle.
explanation.walkthrough: Castle Rackrent (1800) is Maria Edgeworth's novel about an Anglo-Irish estate, so the castle's name is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Castle Rackrent is the fictional Irish seat in Edgeworth's novel, named for exorbitant rents.

clue.text: Improvise in a tricky situation

definitions.meaning: jazz musicians improvise together in an informal session
a fix or predicament, being in a tight spot

explanation.definitionFit: Musicians improvising play together informally; a predicament is also a pickle you are stuck in.

clue.text: Avenger chosen by a supreme deity

parts.note: the elect are those chosen
Ra was the supreme sun god of ancient Egypt

explanation.surface: An avenging hero is picked out by the highest of the gods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link putting the god beside the first piece. Electra avenged her father Agamemnon by helping Orestes kill their mother.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek tragedy Electra seeks revenge for her murdered father, making her an avenger.

clue.text: "We cannot reform our -' (George Eliot)

parts.note: a quotation from George Eliot's Middlemarch with its last word missing: our ancestors cannot be changed

explanation.definitionFit: The missing word completes Eliot's line about the ancestors who shaped us and cannot be altered.

clue.text: Writer's replaced stories with a spot of tea

indicators.note: replaced suggests the letters are put back in new places, a rearrangement
a spot of something is just a small bit, here its first letter

explanation.surface: An author has swapped tales for a little cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' rearranges STORIES into ROSSETI and 'a spot of' adds the T from tea. The 's is a link ('is').
explanation.definitionFit: Christina and Dante Gabriel Rossetti were Victorian poets, so the surname names a writer.

clue.text: One seen in two forms in Tennyson poems

definitions.text: One seen in two forms in Tennyson poems

indicators.note: the same word appears twice in different shapes, once jumbled and once as written

parts.note: taken as written for the second form

explanation.surface: A character appears in two different guises in poems by Tennyson.
explanation.walkthrough: ONE is jumbled to OEN and then written plainly. Tennyson wrote both 'Oenone' and 'The Death of Oenone', so she is one figure seen in two poems.
explanation.definitionFit: Oenone, the nymph abandoned by Paris, is the heroine of two Tennyson poems.

clue.text: Shakespearean soldier with royal badge seen in a Surrey town

indicators.note: seen in places the royal badge pieces inside the name of the town

parts.note: Egham is a town in Surrey, near Runnymede
a pin is a small badge worn on clothing

explanation.surface: A soldier from Shakespeare is spotted wearing a royal emblem in a Surrey town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' puts the royal badge inside the town, just after its first letter. Sir Thomas Erpingham is the old knight in Henry V who lends the king his cloak.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Thomas Erpingham fights at Agincourt in Shakespeare's Henry V, a soldier in the play.

clue.text: Sort of groom embraced by fit Maid Marian?

indicators.note: embraced by means one piece sits wrapped inside the other

parts.note: hale means fit and healthy
to comb hair is one way of grooming it

explanation.surface: A kind of bridegroom is hugged by a fit Maid Marian of Robin Hood fame.
explanation.walkthrough: Not Robin Hood's love: Marian Halcombe is the unmarried heroine of Wilkie Collins's The Woman in White, so the question mark flags a maid named Marian.
explanation.definitionFit: Marian Halcombe is a spinster in Collins's novel, literally a maid called Marian.

clue.text: Explains how sickly poet's entering a competition

indicators.note: entering puts the poet's name inside the word for a contest

parts.note: a cup is a competition, as in the FA Cup
Edward Lear, the nonsense poet, suffered epilepsy and poor health all his life

explanation.surface: Someone sets out how a frail poet comes to be taking part in a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'how' is a link. The answer also describes an illness that goes away, a nod to the sickly poet.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear something up is to make it plain, a phrasal synonym for making clear.

clue.text: I can be seen in Peter Pan can my pet?

definitions.text: I can be seen in Peter Pan

parts.note: can and john are both American slang for a lavatory
darling, like my pet, is a term of endearment

explanation.surface: A speaker asks whether, being able to appear in Peter Pan, a beloved animal can too.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks in the first person: John Darling is Wendy's brother who flies to Neverland in J. M. Barrie's Peter Pan.
explanation.definitionFit: John Darling is one of the Darling children in Barrie's play, a character in it.

clue.text: Fast work made order of disorder

indicators.note: disorder tells us to throw the preceding words into a jumble

explanation.surface: A rapid piece of work brought tidiness out of chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: MADEORDEROF is rearranged. Freedom Road (1944) is a novel by the American writer Howard Fast, so 'Fast' is a surname, not speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Freedom Road is one of Howard Fast's best-known novels, a book by that author.

clue.text: A scruffy socialist, one in revolutionary work in Slough?

indicators.note: in places the whole assembly between the first letter and the rest of the marsh word

parts.note: a slough is a bog, and a fen is marshland

indicators.note: in places the word for one inside the jumbled work
revolutionary suggests upheaval, so the letters of work are churned

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A shabby leftist, one of a revolutionary movement, lives in the Berkshire town of Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns the letters of 'work' into RKOW; the first 'in' holds 'one' inside that, giving RANKOW, and the second 'in' sets it in the marsh. Frank Owen is the house-painter hero of The Ragged Trousered Philanthropists.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Owen, the poor, threadbare hero of Robert Tressell's novel, preaches socialism to his workmates.

clue.text: Beat Amy to bronze

definitions.meaning: to beat someone is to thrash or hide them
The American novelist of The Joy Luck Club
bronze as a verb, to give skin a sun-browned colour

explanation.definitionFit: Thrash, the surname of novelist Amy, and to brown skin in the sun are all senses of the same word.

clue.text: In the Battery, New York, set fire to John Donne's work

indicators.note: In at the start means the fire-setting word goes inside the battery and city letters

parts.note: AA is a common battery size
lit means set fire to

explanation.surface: Someone sets fire to a work by Donne down at the Battery, the park at Manhattan's tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' sets the fire word between the two letters of the battery size. The Battery is also a real park at the tip of Manhattan, which makes the surface convincing. A Litany is a long devotional poem by Donne.
explanation.definitionFit: A Litany is a religious poem by John Donne, one of his works.

clue.text: "Sweet Helen, make me — with a kiss!" (Christopher Marlowe)

definitions.text: "Sweet Helen, make me — with a kiss!" (Christopher Marlowe)

parts.words: "Sweet Helen, make me — with a kiss!" (Christopher Marlowe)
parts.note: Faustus's plea to Helen of Troy in Marlowe's Doctor Faustus with one word blanked: he wants to live forever

explanation.definitionFit: Faustus asks Helen's kiss to make him deathless, the missing word meaning everlasting.

clue.text: Bishop's poem and article that's despatched by priest

parts.note: the is the definite article
a priest is a small club anglers use to kill a caught catch

explanation.surface: A bishop's verses and a newspaper piece that a clergyman has sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: Bishop is the American poet Elizabeth Bishop, not a cleric, and a priest is an angler's club, not a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fish is a well-known poem by Elizabeth Bishop, about a caught grouper set free.

clue.text: Flora the cockney's slim body part, finally widening?

parts.note: a Cockney says thin with an f sound, so slim, thin, becomes fin
the chin is a part of the face

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A Cockney's slender part of the body ends up getting wider.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class Londoner whose accent turns 'th' into 'f'. Flora Finching is Arthur Clennam's garrulous former sweetheart in Dickens's Little Dorrit.
explanation.definitionFit: Flora is the first name of Mrs Finching in Little Dorrit, so the surname completes it.

clue.text: Doubtful about rubbish I ply where Tantalus once ruled?

indicators.note: about means the doubtful word goes round the rest

parts.note: sus is slang for suspicious or doubtful

indicators.note: rubbish as a verb means to trash, so the words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A sceptic doubts the junk that someone peddles, in the land of Tantalus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbish' scrambles I PLY to IPYL and 'about' wraps the slang for doubtful round it. Mount Sipylus in Lydia was the seat of King Tantalus in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Myth places Tantalus's kingdom at Mount Sipylus in Asia Minor, the region he governed.

clue.text: Oriental despot in a fin de siècle novel

definitions.meaning: the ... dynasty has ruled North Korea as dictators
Kipling's novel of 1901, published at the turn of the century

explanation.definitionFit: The North Korean ruling family name and the title of Kipling's Indian novel share one word.

clue.text: Olive's relative, a herb with ahigh price?

parts.note: basil is a culinary herb
a ransom is a high price paid to free a captive

explanation.surface: Something related to the olive, a herb that costs a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: Olive is Olive Chancellor in Henry James's The Bostonians; Basil Ransom is her Mississippi cousin, not a plant related to olives.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil Ransom is Olive Chancellor's cousin in The Bostonians, her kinsman.

clue.text: "- is courteous — no one more: / For time after time he knocks at the door" (Goethe)

definitions.text: "- is courteous — no one more: / For time after time he knocks at the door" (Goethe)

parts.words: "- is courteous — no one more: / For time after time he knocks at the door" (Goethe)
parts.note: Goethe's lines about the advancing years, which call politely again and again until let in

explanation.definitionFit: Goethe personifies the later years of life as a polite caller who keeps knocking.

clue.text: Rowdy pal's silly kind of humour

indicators.note: silly suggests nonsense, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A boisterous friend's daft brand of comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: ROWDYPAL is rearranged; the 's on pal's adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Puns and verbal games are a form of comedy built on language.

clue.text: Coward retreating with intentions lacking heart — or a military hero?

indicators.note: retreating means going back, so the playwright's first name is written backwards

parts.note: Noel Coward was the English playwright and wit

indicators.note: lacking heart drops the middle letter of the word

parts.note: ideas can mean intentions or plans

explanation.surface: Is a cowardly man pulling back from his plans, gutless, or a war hero?
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns NOEL to LEON; 'lacking heart' removes the central E from IDEAS. Leonidas was the Spartan king who held Thermopylae.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonidas led the Spartans at Thermopylae, a celebrated warrior king.

clue.text: Japanese artist seen with 19 in Japanese costume

indicators.note: seen with the other answer, the two together make the costume, so the cross-reference comes off it

parts.note: a kimono is a traditional Japanese robe
the answer to 19 across, the Kipling novel

explanation.surface: A Japanese artist appears with another answer dressed in Japanese clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 across is KIM; put it with this answer and you get KIMONO. Yoko Ono is a Japanese conceptual artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoko Ono is a Japanese-born conceptual and performance artist.

clue.text: Do lesson at last with school on the radio

indicators.note: at last takes the final letter of lesson
on the radio means as heard, a word that sounds like another

parts.note: Eton is the English public school near Windsor

explanation.surface: Finish the class in the end, with the school broadcasting.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton, the famous boarding school, is said like EATEN. 'Do' is the verb as in doing one's hair, to tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: To do a room or one's hair can mean to tidy it, the same as smartening it up.

clue.text: Elizabethan poet with awfully good coinages

indicators.note: awfully suggests something badly done, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A poet of Elizabeth's age made terrible new words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges the letters of 'coinages' into ASCOIGNE, which follow the abbreviation for good. George Gascoigne was a poet and soldier at Elizabeth I's court.
explanation.definitionFit: George Gascoigne wrote verse and plays in the 1570s, a poet of the Elizabethan age.
